plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Exit QQQ, QQQI, and SMH due to downtrends and stop breaches.
Add a new position in MSFT (10%) as a top-quality name.
This plan aims for capital preservation and a large cash buffer.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and trimming concentrated positions, but still carries market exposure.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 1% to reduce overall leverage.
Reduce SPY to 25% to address concentration and meet the mandate.
Exit QQQ, QQQI, and SMH due to downtrends and stop breaches.
Initiate a new position in SNOW (4%) from the strong scanner setups.
This plan balances growth with risk management, maintaining a cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for ~2.5%/month growth, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces leverage and concentration while blending broad index exposure with quality tech, accepting moderate market volatility.

plan: Increase exposure to SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6% to lean into leverage.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Exit QQQ, QQQI, and SMH due to downtrends and stop breaches.
Initiate a new position in SNOW (6%) from the highest-scoring setups.
This plan aims for stretched growth with a smaller cash buffer.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month growth, embracing higher risk for potentially higher returns. It uses and adds leveraged ETFs, which can lead to significant drawdowns and daily decay, requiring strict stop discipline.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero to prioritize income.
Add QQQI to 30% to increase exposure to income-generating ETFs.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Exit QQQ, SMH, and CRWD to reduce high-beta and downtrend exposure.
This plan focuses on steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, prioritizing steady distributions and low drawdown. While aiming for cash-like income, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in market selloffs.
